newsitem.title: USA: Clinton makes balanced budget top priority.
newsitem.headline: Clinton makes balanced budget top priority.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday balancing the federal budget was his top second-term priority and he was inviting bipartisan congressional leaders to a meeting next week to begin mapping an agreement on that.

"Nothing is more fundamental than balancing the budget," Clinton said at his first news conference since winning re-election on Tuesday. "We must keep our economy going steady and strong by balancing the budget in a way that reflects our bipartisan values."

"I am inviting the bipartisan leadership of Congress to meet with me next week here at the White House to discuss how we can develop a plan together to pass a balanced budget to keep our economy going," Clinton said.

U.S. voters returned Republican majorities to both houses of Congress on Tuesday in the same election that returned Democrat Clinton for a second four-year term. Since then both sides have been making conciliatory statements and Clinton continued that trend on Friday.
He said the election had represented a desire of the voters to endorse "the vital center" of American politics and it was time for bipartisan cooperation to fulfil that desire.

Clinton's most prominent clash with the Republican Congress in his first term came late last year when a stalemate over budget-balancing plans led Congress to allow the federal government to shut down twice for lack of funds.
